purpose.summary: Separate strict fixture ceilings from archival local-regtest service history and test cold upstream reconstruction across 5000 native blocks.
scope: Direct child of signed public main 3c84f5d integrated by PR64.
Default immutable native read scope retains height 2000/index 4096; only the joined opted-in service owner selects archival regtest history.
Remove artificial history ceilings only for that service; preserve signed-height arithmetic, local-regtest/unpruned admission, mempool, payload, retained-window and deep-reorg budgets.
Retain all 68 preceding archival native case bodies; add two scope-law cases with 16 assertions.

Add a failure-only timeout trace of allowlisted public case names after stopping the child group; preserve exact success behavior, assertion parsing, the timeout exception and the 60-second process/cleanup law.
Reuse the cold-reconstruction driver with a 5000-block scenario and a separately declared 120-second startup budget; inherited 402-block scenario and 30/60-second deadlines remain unchanged.
exclusions: No mainnet/testnet network admission, activation, consensus change or default-ON service.
No upstream indexer, ALP algorithm, plugin engine, schema or dependency-lock change.
No private reports/history/operator data, server access, deployment, cutover, release, desktop integration or automatic proof promotion.

commands: Build the exact public compiled-out profile with unchanged native prerequisites.
expected_results: The standalone node builds without Chronik linkage and retains all inherited controls.

commands: Build the exact public compiled-in-disabled profile with existing locked Rust inputs and unchanged native prerequisites.
expected_results: The standalone node builds with runtime Chronik disabled by default and retains all inherited controls.

commands: Build the exact public regtest-plugins profile with existing locked Rust inputs and unchanged native prerequisites.
expected_results: The daemon and native fixture build; inherited profiles retain their existing boundaries.

scenarios.command: Run the two-case history-scope native group and all inherited groups; run long_history_service.py against the exact regtest-plugins build.
expected_results: Two scope-law cases and 16 assertions pass; default fixture ceilings and ordinary runtime authority stay closed.
5000 node-accepted blocks precede first index startup, historical ALP/plugin data at height 102 is reconstructed through upstream, the same index reopens in another process and advances to 5001.
failure_conditions: Wrong scope/count, widened network/live-resource budget, height overflow, stale or incomplete historical view, timeout, skip, nonzero exit, source/build drift or failed cleanup.

limitations: A finite 5000-block regtest history is not mainnet historical parity, operator-binary evidence or a production resource guarantee.
Only the joined local-regtest service has archival history scope; strict owned snapshots remain bounded at height 2000 and 4096 indexes.
Signed-height arithmetic excludes INT32_MAX; live reconciliation still retains 288 blocks, caps payload at 64 MiB and mempool at 4096, and refuses deep reorg below its retained anchor.
The positioned-transaction catalogue still has O(height) first-query bootstrap under cs_main; full-history query latency and memory admission remain open.
The new 120-second long-history listener budget is declared separately; inherited 30-second startup waits and 60-second native process deadlines are not increased.
System dependencies remain unlocked; no reproducible-build, continuous-ingress, operator-plugin or mainnet readiness claim.
counterevidence: The local normal regtest-plugins matrix for this lot timed out in capture-and-query-controls at repetition 2 under the unchanged 60-second deadline. No passing complete report exists for that run; later diagnostic observations cannot replace it.
Historical startup and aggregate stop/reopen timeouts and upstream dependency alerts remain open.
No mainnet datadir, server comparison, deployment or operator cutover is exercised.
